newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus bars official from U.S. Soros foundation.
newsitem.headline: Belarus bars official from U.S. Soros foundation.

text.p: Belarus has accused the local executive director of the Soros Foundation of supporting the opposition and barred him from re-entering the country, state-run television said on Monday.
The foundation, set up by American billionaire George Soros, has invested $13 million in Belarus, including $6 million last year mostly for education, ecological and medical programmes.
The television said Peter Bern, a U.S. citizen, was accused by authorities of interfering in Belarussian domestic affairs and was barred "for activities that do not correspond to his status".

The television presenter added that Bern was accused of taking part in mass actions organised by the opposition and aired pictures, provided by the KGB security service, showing him watching a recent opposition rally from the sidelines.
"The barring of the opposition's best friend will not mean any difficulties for the Soros Foundation's activities in Belarus," the TV presenter said.
"But lists of the people who have been given grants from this foundation will be published soon and (the Belarussian) people will know who they are," he added.
Bern, who is based in Minsk, arrived on Sunday afternoon from a meeting in Budapest of the foundation's executive directors from Central and Eastern Europe.

"We intended to meet Bern at the airport but were barred from doing so. They didn't even allow us to talk to him," said Roman Yakovlevsky, a Belarussian member of the foundation's management in Minsk.
Yakovlevsky said that Bern was due to depart to Frankfurt on Monday afternoon but there were no information whether he had already been deported to Germany.

"I think the authorities want to adapt the Soros Foundation to the rules established by Belarus's regime," Yakovlevsky said. "We have been under pressure for quite a long time to stop support (in grants) to the independent mass media."

U.S. ambassador to Belarus Kenneth Yalovitz cancelled a visit to Grodno on the Polish border where he intended to take part in the ceremony marking the opening of housing for military servicemen built with American financial help.
"The embassy thinks that Belarus violated international norms," said Alexei Solomakha, embassy spokesman. "We were not informed about the incident and had no chance to communicate with Bern."
Solomakha added that ambassador Yalovitz would meet Foreign Minister Ivan Antonovich later on Monday to express dissatisfaction with the incident.
